articles.title: Celtic deficiencies laid bare at LASK on another night of Champions League pain
articles.summary: When Callum McGregor eviscerated his own team-mates in the wake of Celtic's stupefying Champions League collapse against LASK, he delivered their one coherent moment of a spineless night, writes Tom English.
articles.body:
When Callum McGregor eviscerated his own team-mates in the wake of Celtic's stupefying Champions League collapse against LASK, he delivered their one coherent moment of a spineless night.

In branding his fellow players "passive" and "scared" and in then sending a telling shot across their bows - "now we'll see what people are made of" - it is hard to recall him being so full of fury after a European game.

And there are plenty to choose from, plenty of dark nights, plenty of embarrassment, plenty of soul-searching over many years.

For close to a decade he has been Celtic's best player, a near ever-present. That longevity has brought him many trophies, but he's been around for many mortifications, too.

Where losing a 4-0 advantage ranks in the pantheon of Celtic failures is a moot point. What is unarguable is that it was a total capitulation, a feeble collapse in the face of LASK's physicality and desire and belief.

O'Neill takes responsibility after Celtic's latest European capitulation Published 9 hours ago

O'Neill takes responsibility after Celtic's latest European capitulation

Exhausted & fragile - how Celtic's capitulation unfolded Published 9 hours ago

Exhausted & fragile - how Celtic's capitulation unfolded

Celtic blow four-goal lead to LASK in Champions League collapse

The Celtic captain called his players "scared" when winning 4-0. No media hatchet man could come up with a more damaging word to describe what happened out there.

McGregor has been through the European mill.

He was there last season when Celtic's fecklessness saw them go goalless for 210 minutes against the popgun boys of Kairat Almaty before failing to score from three of their five penalties in the shootout.

He was there for the 7-1 against Borussia Dortmund and the 6-0 against Atletico Madrid.

He's a survivor of the Champions League play-off exit to Midtjylland and the pair of 4-1 losses to Sparta Prague in the Europa League.

He was around for earlier Champions League play-off exits against Ferencvaros, AEK Athens and Cluj.

He's a veteran of the 7-1 loss to PSG and the 7-0 loss to Barcelona. He wears the scars as much as he holds the medals.

It is difficult, though, to recall him being as seething as he was on Tuesday night.

He wasn't ranting - that is not his style. He spoke calmly which lent his words more power.

He was raging in his own way. Raging at another exit, raging that when the chips were down too many of his fellow players panicked and allowed themselves to be overrun, raging at professional pride being trampled underfoot for all to see.

'Rabbits in headlights don't look as lost as Celtic did'

It was McGregor who opened the scoring on the night, a deflected shot and a 4-0 lead on aggregate.

LASK had started well but that goal looked to all the world like a kick to their solar plexus. They had chances in Glasgow and they had chances in the opening minutes in Linz - and they were 4-0 down!

How many punches can one team take before they lose their fight? Many, as it turned out.

Celtic were obliging, of course. Painfully so. We trumpeted their classy goals and their adventurous play a week ago and wrongly assumed that they had gumption to go with it. Big mistake.

When Benjamin Nygren's ridiculously loose pass led directly to LASK's equaliser on the night, the first signs of a wobble were visible.

Thirty two minutes had been played and Celtic did not look wholly comfortable at 4-1 on aggregate. Mad, but true.

When they conceded again three minutes into the second half, there were a few jelly legs on show. Auston Trusty was culpable this time. Brushed off the ball. Swatted and 4-2 now.

Trusty was poor, not the only one, but a point of real weakness that LASK went for.

Ten minutes after the hosts scored their second, they scored their third. Too many parts of the Celtic team were in full fright mode now. The slow death was picking up pace.

Camilo Duran, the hero of the first leg, was reduced to a non-event. Kasper Hogh worked hard but with no impact. Passes went astray. Celtic were directionless. Everything fell apart.

Rabbits in headlights do not tend to look as lost as Celtic did when the pressure really hit.

If McGregor was trying to put out fires in his own team he was failing. He could not cut through the tension.

Martin O'Neill looked on like a man 10 years older than his true age. This was a shocking night for him. One of his worst in football, he said later. He took responsibility, but he cannot be alone in that.

He emptied his bench in a desperate attempt to stem the flow, but his substitutions, five in 12 befuddled minutes, had zero impact.

Celtic did not have a shot on target in the second half of normal time nor in extra-time. They only existed as a man hanging off a cliff edge exists. There was only one way this was going to end.

LASK's fourth goal might have come in the 90th minute but it was deserved.

By that point they'd had 33 shots on Celtic's goal (they finished on 40) to go with the 20 from last week. It was a rout.

Cameron Carter-Vickers was hobbling about on one leg. Hogh much the same. Forward came the waves and Celtic tried to hold them back with a back four of Anthony Ralston, Dane Murray, Trusty and Liam Scales.

The fifth goal was a mercy, and another Celtic player doing the wrong thing at the wrong time in the wrong place. For Nygren and Trusty read Luke McCowan. Hapless and helpless - and out of the Champions League.

'Celtic ambition will be questioned again'

The night meandered to its conclusion. LASK missed a penalty for 6-1 before Miguel Freckleton, recently of St Mirren, slalomed his way into the Celtic box and threatened, for a second, to score.

All credit to Freckleton and his new beginning in Austria, but in flashes he was made to look like a serious player in his few minutes on the pitch. When that kind of thing happens it tells a story.

Celtic were beyond disarray by then. Spooked, over-powered, out-fought, out-played. The smooth-running killers of last week in Glasgow was an optical illusion that hid psychological deficiencies.

Nobody could have predicted that they would fall in such a heap at 4-0, but they did.

Celtic, quite obviously, need a back-up left-back to Kieran Tierney and they don't have one.

They absolutely need, and this is no secret, a physical presence in the middle of the pitch, a player of stature in every sense of the word, a guy who would not be bullied as Celtic were bullied in Austria. They don't have one of those either.

They have done good deals but not enough of them. They're in net profit in their transfer business this summer.

The A-word - ambition - is going to get another airing. When you finish a £40m match with a back four of Ralston, Murray, Trusty and Scales then, as a club, you have not done your work properly. Nobody did on the night, on the field and off.

All those other defeats were incredibly costly in a financial but also in a self-worth sense.

They hoped they'd left the Champions League drawing board behind, but they're right back where they were when Kairat and Midtjylland and Ferencvaros and Cluj and AEK were the ones inflicting the pain.

Incredibly, another name has to get added to the list.

Ten minutes after the hosts scored their second, they scored their third. Too many parts of the Celtic team were in full fright mode now. The slow death was picking up pace.

Camilo Duran, the hero of the first leg, was reduced to a non-event. Kasper Hogh worked hard but with no impact. Passes went astray. Celtic were directionless. Everything fell apart. Rabbits in headlights don't tend to look as lost as Celtic did when the pressure really hit.

If McGregor was trying to put out fires in his own team he was failing. He could not cut through the tension.

Martin O'Neill looked on like a man 10 years older than his true age. This was a shocking night for him. One of his worst in football, he said later. He took responsibility, but he can't be alone in that.

He emptied his bench in a desperate attempt to stem the flow, but his substitutions, five in 12 befuddled minutes, had zero impact.

Celtic did not have a shot on target in the second half of normal time nor in extra-time. They only existed as a man hanging off a cliff edge exists. There was only one way this was going to end.

LASK's fourth goal might have come in the 90th minute but it was deserved.

By that point they'd had 33 shots on Celtic's goal (they finished on 40) to go with the 20 from last week. It was a rout.

Cameron Carter-Vickers was hobbling about on one leg. Hogh much the same. Forward came the waves and Celtic tried to hold them back with a back four of Anthony Ralston , Dane Murray , Trusty and Liam Scales .

The fifth goal was a mercy, and another Celtic player doing the wrong thing at the wrong time in the wrong place. For Nygren and Trusty read Luke McCowan . Hapless and helpless - and out of the Champions League.

'Celtic ambition will be questioned again'

The night meandered to its conclusion. LASK missed a penalty for 6-1 before Miguel Freckleton, recently of St Mirren, slalomed his way into the Celtic box and threatened, for a second, to score.

All credit to Freckleton and his new beginning in Austria , but in flashes he was made to look like a serious player in his few minutes on the pitch. When that kind of things happens it tells a story.

Celtic were beyond disarray by then. Spooked, over-powered, out-fought, out-played. The smooth-running killers of last week in Glasgow was an optical illusion that hid psychological deficiencies. Nobody could have predicted that they would fall in such a heap at 4-0, but they did.

Celtic, quite obviously, need a back-up left-back to Kieran Tierney and they don't have one.

They absolutely need, and this is no secret, a physical presence in the middle of the pitch, a player of stature in every sense of the word, a guy who would not be bullied as Celtic were bullied in Austria. They don't have one of those either.

They have done good deals but not enough of them. They're in net profit in their transfer business this summer.

The A word - ambition - is going to get another airing. When you finish a £40m match with a back four of Ralston, Murray, Trusty and Scales then, as a club, you have not done your work properly. Nobody did on the night, on the field and off.

All those other defeats were incredibly costly in a financial but also in a self-worth sense.

They hoped they'd left the Champions League drawing board behind, but they're right back where they were when Kairat and Midtjylland and Ferencvaros and Cluj and AEK were the ones inflicting the pain.

Incredibly, another name has to get added to the list.

articles.title: Liverpool star expected to depart for La Liga
articles.summary: Stefan Bajcetic Near Celta Vigo Transfer as Liverpool Agree Future Sale DealLiverpool are closing in on an agreement that will see Stefan Bajcetic join Celta...
articles.body:
Stefan Bajcetic Near Celta Vigo Transfer as Liverpool Agree Future Sale Deal

Liverpool are closing in on an agreement that will see Stefan Bajcetic join Celta Vigo on a permanent transfer, with the structure of the deal now becoming clear. As first reported by Matteo Moretto , the Spain youth international is on the verge of completing the move and is expected to undergo a medical shortly.

The terms are particularly noteworthy. Rather than a sizeable upfront fee, Liverpool have agreed a package based largely on bonuses, while also securing a percentage of any future sale. That approach suggests Anfield decision-makers still see long term value in the midfielder, even if his pathway under Andoni Iraola now appears limited.

The speed of developments points to a deal in its final stages. It was further explained that Celta and Liverpool have reached an agreement which gives the Merseyside club a sell-on interest, with the move carrying almost no immediate cost beyond bonuses and that future percentage.

For Celta Vigo, this looks like a low-risk opportunity to sign a player who, at his best, has shown composure, tactical intelligence and quality in possession. For Liverpool, it reflects a modern transfer strategy, accepting a modest short-term return in exchange for protection if the player rediscovers his highest level in La Liga.

Liverpool Sell-On Clause Offers Protection

Sell-on clauses are increasingly common in deals involving young players whose development has stalled at elite clubs. In Bajcetic's case, Liverpool appear to have chosen flexibility over a fixed transfer fee, which may suit all parties. Celta Vigo gain an affordable addition, while Liverpool retain a financial stake in the player's future progress.

The expectation now is that the medical will follow soon, barring any late complication. Once completed, it will mark another notable exit in a summer of continued reshaping at Anfield.

From a Liverpool supporter's perspective, this one feels genuinely sad. Bajcetic always looked like the kind of midfielder fans could really connect with, calm on the ball, brave in the challenge and smart beyond his years. There was a spell when it felt as though Liverpool had uncovered a major long-term answer in the middle of the pitch, someone who could grow into a huge role.

That is why this report lands with a bit of disappointment. Even if the logic of the deal makes sense financially, and even if the sell-on clause gives Liverpool some protection, it is hard to ignore the feeling that a talented young player is leaving before his story at Anfield truly got going. Supporters will naturally wonder whether patience might have been rewarded.

There is also the emotional side of it. Fans invest in academy-linked talents because they represent possibility, identity and continuity. Seeing Bajcetic move on for a deal with very little guaranteed money makes it feel more like Liverpool are cutting their losses than cashing in on a developed asset.

Hopefully, if this goes through, he thrives in Spain and Liverpool are proven wise to keep a future stake. Even so, many supporters will watch this one unfold with regret, because Bajcetic always seemed like he had the tools to make a real impact in red.

articles.title: Fernandes wins prestigious PFA award
articles.summary: Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes was named the Professional Footballers' Associations Men's Player of the Year at the PFA awards.  Fernandes, who la...
articles.body:
Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes was named the Professional Footballers' Associations Men's Player of the Year at the PFA awards.

Fernandes, who last season broke the record for the most assists in a single Premier League campaign with 21, is the first United player to win the award since Wayne Rooney in 2010.

Although it was another trophy-less campaign for Manchester United, Fernandes enjoyed individual success, surpassing Kevin de Bruyne and Thierry Henry 's record of 20 assists in a Premier League campaign.

Fernandes set up his side's opener on the final day of the season against Brighton – and scored their third – to finish 2025-26 with nine goals and 21 assists in 35 league outings. Man City 's Rayan Cherki was the second-most prolific provider, with 12 assists.

His haul helped United finish third and secure Champions League football.

In total, the 31-year-old scored nine goals and contributed 22 assists in 37 matches in all competitions.

Fernandes, who joined the club from Sporting Lisbon in January 2020, beat Arsenal trio Gabriel Magalhaes, David Raya , and Declan Rice and Man City attackers Cherki and Erling Haaland to the award.

He is only the second Portuguese to be named player of the year, following back-to-back wins for former United winger Cristiano Ronaldo in 2007 and 2008.

articles.title: Mourinho’s nickname for Real Madrid hero Carlos Espí after Espanyol impact
articles.summary: Carlos Espi may have only recently arrived at Real Madrid, but the young striker has already made a telling impact at the club, and it appears Jose Mourinho...
articles.body:
Carlos Espi may have only recently arrived at Real Madrid , but the young striker has already made a telling impact at the club, and it appears Jose Mourinho has found a special way of describing his new protege.

After Espi emerged as one of Real Madrid's heroes in the match against Espanyol , Mourinho used his post-match press conference to explain the tactical thinking behind the youngster's introduction.

In doing so, the Real Madrid manager revealed the nickname he has already given the 1.94-metre forward: " El gigante " (the giant).

It is a nickname that perfectly sums up Espi's physical profile and the role Mourinho believes he can play for Real Madrid.

The former Levante striker offers a very different option in attack, and his appearance against Espanyol showed exactly why the Portuguese coach sees value in having him available.

Why Espi was introduced against Espanyol

Carlos Espi scored the winning goal vs Espanyol. (Photo by Alex Caparros/Getty Images)

Speaking about the decision to bring Espi into the game, Mourinho pointed to the difficulties Kylian Mbappé was facing as Real Madrid searched for a breakthrough.

Mbappe had begun dropping deeper in an attempt to collect possession and create individual situations, looking to take on defenders and unlock the opposition himself.

Mourinho felt a more physical presence could change the dynamic and help stretch the Espanyol defence. Hence, Espi was brought on to provide precisely that.

"Kylian (Mbappe), already at his wits' end, was trying to drop back, get the ball and create a one-on-one situation, trying to beat one or two players.

"I thought Carlos could be important there to pin the opponent in place. With Trent on the pitch, the quality of crosses improves massively too, and having 'the giant' there could also be a solution," said the manager.

Mourinho has a nickname for Carlos Espi. (Photo by Alex Caparros/Getty Images)

Mourinho summed up that idea with his newly revealed nickname, referring to Espi simply as "the giant."

The relationship between Mourinho and Espi has developed since the striker arrived at Real Madrid.

The pair even live in the same residence complex in Valdebebas, creating an unusually close connection between the manager and his young forward despite the fact that they have known each other for only a relatively short period.

That proximity has seemingly helped Mourinho understand the player's personality and qualities quickly.

Espi has also been able to learn closely from one of football's most experienced managers as he begins the next stage of his career.

articles.title: Lamine Yamal unhappy at Barcelona – here’s what has upset the young star
articles.summary: Barcelona’s emphatic 5-0 victory over Elche should have been a night of celebration, but Lamine Yamal’s reaction after being substituted created an unexpecte...
articles.body:
Barcelona 's emphatic 5-0 victory over Elche should have been a night of celebration, but Lamine Yamal 's reaction after being substituted created an unexpected talking point.

According to SPORT , the Barcelona forward is unhappy with the situation surrounding close friend Alejandro Balde , with the uncertainty around several players from his inner circle affecting his mood.

Yamal was substituted by Hansi Flick in the 65th minute against Elche and appeared visibly serious as he made his way to the bench.

Images of the teenager sitting with a sombre expression prompted questions about whether there was a deeper issue behind his reaction, particularly after he remained affected despite attempts from teammates to lift his spirits.

Now, one account has offered a possible explanation, and it has little to do with Yamal's performances on the pitch.

Barcelona were dominant at the Martínez Valero, beginning the new season with a convincing 5-0 win.

Yet, Yamal did not enjoy his strongest performance and his substitution became one of the most closely discussed moments of the match.

Lamine, Casado and Balde share a great friendship. (Photo by Alex Caparros/Getty Images)

The young forward's expression after leaving the pitch was noticeably serious, and it did not change during the remainder of the evening. That naturally led to speculation about his state of mind.

Now, Barcelona pundit Jota Jordi has dismissed suggestions that Yamal's mood is connected to his form or disappointment surrounding the World Cup and Ballon d'Or discussions.

Instead, he believes the explanation lies much closer to home.

Lamine affected by Balde, Casado and Hector Fort situations

According to Jota Jordi, Yamal has been particularly affected by the uncertainty surrounding three of his closest friends at Barcelona: Balde, Marc Casado and Hector Fort .

The pundit claimed that the situations involving the three players have unfolded within a short period, with Balde's recent circumstances followed by uncertainty over Casado and Fort.

"He's a 19-year-old lad and his three best friends of the last ten years are leaving, and I can assure you that's why. Don't look for any other reasons," Jota Jordi said.

"It's solely and exclusively because the Balde situation happened 24 hours earlier, Casado is also slipping out the back door, and then there's the matter of Héctor Fort," he added.

Balde's future is uncertain at Barcelona. (Photo by Judit Cartiel/Getty Images)

The claim should be treated as the pundit's account of the situation rather than an official explanation from Yamal or Barcelona.

Neither the player nor the club has publicly confirmed why the forward appeared upset after the Elche match.

Close friendships make Barcelona departures difficult

Yamal is particularly close to the trio and had hoped to share what could be an exciting season at Barcelona with them.

In fact, Jota Jordi described the three players as being like "brothers" to Yamal and suggested that the possibility of their departures has taken an emotional toll on the Barcelona star.

"They're his brothers, and they tell me Lamine feels bad about it because he thinks it's going to be a great season and that, with three Barça fans like these three, he's going to miss out on what's to come. I can assure you that's more or less how it is," he added.

Balde's situation remains particularly relevant, with recent reports suggesting that his role under Flick has become less secure.

Casado and Fort have also faced uncertainty regarding their respective futures.

Premier League history was made before a ball was even kicked this season as a record nine clubs started the campaign with new managers.

The post-Andoni Iraola has begun at Bournemouth under new head coach Marco Rose, who last managed RB Leipzig in the Bundesliga.

So how did he fare on an eventful first weekend of the 2026-27 campaign?

The German successor came within six minutes of starting his Premier League career with a statement win at Manchester City , only to concede two late goals to suffer a heartbreaking loss.

He will be frustrated at the manner of City's goals, with Marc Guehi unmarked at a corner for the equaliser, then a slow reaction for Josko Gvardiol's stoppage-time winner, but Rose was also shown in those first 84 minutes that he has plenty of materials to work with in a Cherries side that finished sixth last season.

Rose will have seen enough to deliver early signs of encouragement amid the disappointment of such a painful late loss.

articles.title: How did Iraola fare on his Liverpool managerial debut?
articles.summary: Premier League history was made before a ball was even kicked this season as a record nine clubs started the campaign with new managers.  Former Bournemouth...
articles.body:
Premier League history was made before a ball was even kicked this season as a record nine clubs started the campaign with new managers.

Former Bournemouth boss Andoni Iraola got his first taste of action as Liverpool manager after succeeding sacked Arne Slot.

So how did he fare on an eventful first weekend of the 2026-27 campaign?

Iraola was spared the ignominy of defeat in his first Premier League game since succeeding Slot by Dominik Szoboszlai 's 99th-minute penalty - but this was a sobering fact-finding mission for the new man in charge at Anfield.

He did not seem unduly concerned, but both of Newcastle United 's goals will have been hauntingly familiar to those who watched Liverpool's title defence collapse under Slot last season.

The Magpies cashed in on Liverpool's wide open midfield, a flaw from the last campaign that saw them so vulnerable to fast counter-attacks.

Anthony Elanga sliced through Liverpool for the first, then six of Iraola's team stood idly by as Yoane Wissa and Joe Willock combined for the second.

Iraola has suggested Liverpool will not strengthen in midfield with a number six-type defensively minded player. This early evidence - not to mention what was seen last season - suggests they should.

If not, the draw at Newcastle was a red flag showing Iraola needs to find an internal solution which is not currently obvious.

It is all very well targeting wide players such as Bradley Barcola and Yankuba Minteh , but what about when teams are running straight through the heart of Liverpool's team?

Iraola must also find a way to make the subdued Alexander Isak and Florian Wirtz look like the players Liverpool paid a combined £241m for. Both were poor again at St James' Park.

articles.title: How Savinho brings a different route forward
articles.summary: Savinho's involvement for Manchester City fell sharply last season after the club signed winger Antoine Semenyo from Bournemouth in January.  Savinho registe...
articles.body:
Savinho 's involvement for Manchester City fell sharply last season after the club signed winger Antoine Semenyo from Bournemouth in January.

He played 821 Premier League minutes, scoring once and providing one assist, while featuring in only 31% of City's available minutes.

That was a significant drop from the previous campaign, when he played 54%.

Yet his 2024-25 numbers show why Tottenham are prepared to invest heavily in him. Savinho registered eight Premier League assists that season, all from open play, despite playing only 1,773 minutes. Only five players recorded more from open play.

On a per-90 basis, he ranked third for open-play assists with 0.41, while only Mohamed Salah created more chances per 90 than Savinho's 2.2.

His biggest threat, though, came from carrying the ball. Among Premier League players with at least 1,000 minutes in 2024-25, only Jeremy Doku averaged more progressive carries of at least 10 metres than Savinho's 6.8 per 90.

Savinho also led the division for carries followed by a chance created, averaging 1.3 per 90, while only Son Heung-min ended a carry with an assist more frequently.

He completed 2.6 dribbles per 90 with a 51% success rate and used those carries to draw defenders towards him before releasing team-mates.

That ability was even more evident during his breakout season at Girona . Savinho played 2,989 minutes in La Liga in 2023-24, with 65% of them coming on the left wing. He scored nine goals, supplied eight assists and established himself as one of the division's most dangerous one-against-one players.

At City, his role shifted. Across his two Premier League seasons, his most common position was on the right, accounting for 36% of his minutes, compared to 20% on the left. That versatility could matter at Spurs.

articles.title: Man United’s Fernandes, City’s Shaw named PFA Players of the Year
articles.summary: Fernandes rewarded for an outstanding season with a record number of assists in the league; Shaw builds on league win and Golden Boot.
articles.body:
Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes was crowned the Professional Footballers’ Association (PFA) Player of the Year, while Manchester City’s Khadija Shaw scooped the Women’s award for the second time.

The award wins on Tuesday highlighted the individual brilliance of both players, with contrasting fortunes for their respective teams during the season.

Portuguese international Fernandes broke the Premier League assists record during an outstanding 2025–26 season, setting up 21 goals as he surpassed Thierry Henry and Kevin De Bruyne’s previous mark.

The 31-year-old also scored nine times as United overcame a poor start to finish third in the Premier League under Michael Carrick and earned a return to the Champions League.

Fernandes also won the Football Writers’ Association Footballer of the Year award in May.

“It is obviously a very proud moment. They are the ones you go on the pitch against, and it’s probably not easy to vote for someone you play against, so it is a very good moment,” said Fernandes.

Shaw was rewarded for scoring 21 goals on the way to a third straight Golden Boot and securing City’s first Women’s Super League title in a decade.

City also saw further success as Nico O’Reilly was named Men’s Young Player of the Year.

The 21-year-old scored twice in the League Cup final as City beat Arsenal and was part of the side that also won the FA Cup last season.

“I’m very proud of the season I had,” said the England international. “I won two trophies with my club and managed to play at the World Cup with my country. I’m over the moon with how it turned out.”

O’Reilly was joined by City teammates Erling Haaland, Rayan Cherki and Antoine Semenyo in the Team of the Year.

Champions Arsenal had five representatives in David Raya, Gabriel, William Saliba, Jurrien Timber and Declan Rice, with Fernandes and Brentford’s Igor Thiago completing the XI.

articles.title: Irish League: What is the relationship between gambling and football in Northern Ireland?
articles.summary: From changing culture to investment and criticism, BBC Sport NI examines the Irish League's ever-changing relationship with gambling.
articles.body:
Looking back at his 20-year career in the Irish League, Aaron Hogg remembers the first time he went to the bookies with his team-mates.

A teenager at the time, he did not know the journey it would set him upon. It was a road of debt, broken relationships and severe depression.

The goalkeeper was not the first Irish League player to have a gambling addiction, and he will not be the last.

But now, eight years since he last placed a bet, he is at the heart of an initiative to try and help those who need it through the new player-led Gambling Support Group (GSG).

Its introduction coincides with increased sponsorship of the men's and women's Irish Premiership from betting companies from this season, while the two League Cups and a regional tournament are also sponsored by bookmakers.

From culture to investment and criticism, BBC Sport NI examines the Irish League's relationship with gambling.

How Premier League shirts will change with gambling sponsor ban Published 13 August

How Premier League shirts will change with gambling sponsor ban

When Hogg started gambling it was for fun, with fruit machines and playing pool as a teenager.

When he stepped into men's football with Crusaders, he would start to go to the bookies with team-mates before matches.

Then he was introduced to hose racing and roulette. Things spiralled from there.

"Gambling's a progressive illness," he said.

"You don't just start off by doing a bet and then all of a sudden you lose your house."

Ultimately, playing football became his "release".

"It was brilliant because my head was completely concentrated on that game and everything else went away, I was at peace for 90 minutes.

"But then I walked back into the dressing room, and as soon as you sit back down your world comes back down on top of you.

"As a gambler, you don't deal with any of your problems. You shy away from everybody, and you try and get more and more money to gamble and dig yourself deeper and deeper in the hole."

The Irish FA's betting regulations in Northern Ireland say that players cannot bet on any matches involving their team - at men's, women's or underage level - or league, and no one can place a bet on their behalf.

Michael Carvill, head of the Professional Footballers' Association in Northern Ireland, said it was something he had noticed in a 15-year career at the top of the Irish League.

The PFA are working with the Irish FA and former players with the Gambling Support Group, where support and education are key.

Carvill relates to his former Crusaders team-mate Matthew Snoddy, who is one of four players involved in the GSG alongside Hogg, Aaron Traynor and Michael Ruddy.

"I sat beside Matthew for seven years and I never knew he had an issue," said Carvill, who added you could see players' moods change whenever they checked their phones immediately after games.

"It's something that is concerning when you think you can share a changing room, train with them three nights a week and play with them and you're not aware of what's going on.

"It's really a wake-up call for all of us that this isn't going away. We have to set up something to try and treat it, and that's the purpose of this project."

As Carvill points out, gambling goes far beyond the traditional forms of betting - something he says has "increased risk".

He touches on prize websites and competitions on TV, and says it is even being found in the academy levels of the game in Northern Ireland through gaming and in-game purchases.

Across his career in the Irish League, which started in 2006, Hogg witnessed first hand how the gambling industry changed, and how that impacted players.

While you used to have to go into the bookies to physically place a bet, with smartphones you can now gamble 24/7, and on endless things.

"The markets are now more advanced. It's now become, like roulette, it's almost instant," he said.

"Betting habits have changed. Back then, when I started, there was more a social aspect to it.

"There's just so much accessibility now that it is becoming more and more prevalent to footballers."

From the start of this season, betting sponsorship is banned on the front of shirts in England in the Premier League, but still allowed on sleeves and training kits.

The ban, which was voluntarily voted for by clubs, meant eight sides had to find new front of sh i rt sponsors for the upcoming season.

Things are different in the Championship in England, where there are not the same restrictions, and in Scotland, where the SPL is sponsored by a betting company and both champions Celtic and rivals Rangers currently have betting companies on the front of their shirts.

In the Irish Premiership, three clubs - Glentoran, Cliftonville and Crusaders - are all sponsored by betting companies on the front of their shirts, while Linfield have one on their sleeve and champions Larne have it on the backs of their shirts.

Crusaders carry their betting sponsor in the Women's Premiership, while Glentoran's Oval ground in east Belfast also carries the name of a betting company.

The league's new sponsorship deal with a bookmakers also means that the betting company will be on the sleeves of players, on sponsor boards and player of the match trophies, and on the league's social media branding.

One match, over 5,000 gambling ads - is 'ban' really working? Published 8 October 2025

One match, over 5,000 gambling ads - is 'ban' really working?

Hooked on risk - gambling's grip on elite sport Published 23 May 2023

Hooked on risk - gambling's grip on elite sport

Tommy Canning is in a unique position. He has coached in both the Irish League and in the League of Ireland, and also in both the men's and women's games.

His day job is as head of treatment at Northlands Addiction Clinic, which deals with issues involving alcohol, drugs and gambling.

When the deal for Boyle Sports to sponsor the Irish Premiership was announced, NIFL says the deal was "the league's first partnership valued at more than £1m".

Canning is critical of the move to have increased gambling sponsorship within the league, and says "what's the cost?" at the expense of increased investment.

He questioned if there were "no other avenues" available to being investment into the league.

"I'm not naive and I understand that without the right sponsorship, nothing can really develop their product.

"But it's disappointing that somewhere in the midst of this, that the integrity doesn't take over from the investment in the product.

"In terms of these sponsorship deals, they are highly lucrative and that can make it difficult for organisations to turn them down.

"But the question that I have asked in the past, and I would ask again, is at what cost are you happy to accept these lucrative deals?

"I think football clubs have a huge role socially and at a community level within the island of Ireland, and they have a responsibility to maintain some levels of integrity in terms of this issue."

Canning said, when you "understand the power of advertising", that it was "irresponsible of organisations like NIFL to be going down this road".

He added it was a "huge concern", and points to how the advertisement of tobacco and alcohol have been banned in sport, and says something similar should happen with gambling.

"There's a direct correlation between advertising and sales, and gambling is the same," he said.

"Although you're not buying anything in terms of physical thing, the impact or the correlation between the advertising of it and somebody then beginning to buy that product are very substantial in terms of the money that's spent.

"Now, not everyone is going to get into trouble, but if more people are doing it and it's more accessible, then the equation of that is that more people are going to get into trouble."

NIFL said, as part of the deal, that Boyle Sports "will launch a responsible gambling awareness initiative across NIFL clubs, using the league's matchday and digital platforms to promote practical information, encourage safer betting conversations and support fans throughout the season".

"I think there's a huge amount of hypocrisy in that statement that 'we're going to take money from betting companies, but you know what? We're going to help you more when you get into trouble'," Canning added.

"I think that's a crazy statement to make, and that's a wee bit about trying to soften the acceptance of the sponsorship. I think that there's huge hypocrisy in it."

The Northern Ireland Football League declined to comment when contacted by BBC Sport.

The Gambling Support Group is the first support group in relation to that form of addiction in the Irish League.

The fact you only have to send a text or scan a QR code, rather than pick up the phone, is a small yet important detail, and information on how to get in touch have been made available in every ground in the Irish Premiership.

"When I was gambling, I was very alone.. I pushed away my wife, my kids," continued Hogg.

"My mum and dad didn't speak to me for a couple of years. You destroy relationships and gambling destroys families.

"Sitting in the house on your own when you've lost everything, and it's just you and your own thoughts - which can be really deep, dark thoughts and depressed - the last thing you want to do is pick the phone up and speak to somebody.

"But to just pick up and text is less personal, and nobody else will have to know."

Hogg said that he can relate to any players who are struggling, and says there "will be no judgement or no shock factor".

"I'll understand everything they're talking about and I can relate to that.

"I haven't had a bet in eight years and my life has turned around full circle. I've got my relationships back, I feel good and I can offer help.

"There is hope and there is life for anybody out there that is struggling with gambling. It doesn't have to be your life."

Carvill added that the GSG is about support, not punishment, which he feels does not tackle the issue and can sometimes make things worse for those affected.

"The good thing about the PFA, which is probably different than the Irish FA, we're not the police, so to speak.

"We're not going to sanction you or punish you or tell you what you're doing is wrong. That's not our role.

"Our role is you can speak to us. It stays with us and we have to get you help."

While the vast majority of gambling issues are in men, women are not immune from addiction issues.

While the four players involved in the GSG played in the men's game, Carvill says that building relationships is key in the Women's Premiership.

"If you don't have a relationship, they're not going to speak to you. You have to connect with them before you can correct them, as I always say.

"Just because it hasn't been promoted as much, in terms of what's been shared about issues, it doesn't mean it's not happening in the women's game."

Carvill said that "one of the most concerning things" is that there is not a gambling commission in Northern Ireland, which limits regulation and the influence that can be had at government level.

For the PFA and GSG, it is about making an impact where they can.

"We are hoping to help, that's our responsibility. Ours is not to change the landscape.

"Ours is to help support the players that are in crisis and obviously prevent the next batch of young players stepping into that dressing room."

The GSG is initially being launched as a one-year scheme with QR codes and posters dotted throughout grounds, but Carvill and Hogg both hope it turns into something more long term.

Hogg says he is "not cured and not fixed" and, while he admits he will have a gambling addiction for the rest of my life, he now has the tools to help him with his recovery.

"In this world, you're never going to escape gambling, whether it be at football, whether it be at work, whether it be at driving," he said.

Even the biggest critics of gambling in football are not naive enough to know it will simply disappear, and that is why Carvill wants the GSG to become an expanded resource.

"If we're coming out and saying there's an issue and there's a problem, but we're not providing a service to support our members, then we're doing a disservice to footballers in Northern Ireland," Carvill said.

"It would be great if we didn't need it, but the reality is we are going to need it.

"It's up to us to make sure we have it in place so that moving forward, we can continue to educate and help players that are struggling."

If you have been affected by issues raised in this article, there is information and support available on BBC Action Line.

articles.title: Raheem Sterling charged with dangerous driving after crash on M3 in Hampshire
articles.summary: Raheem Sterling will appear in court next month to face charges of dangerous driving after crashing his car into motorway barriers in May.
articles.body:
Raheem Sterling will appear in court next month to face charges of dangerous driving and possessing nitrous oxide for wrongful inhalation after crashing his car into motorway barriers in May.

The former England winger, who most recently played for Feyenoord in the Dutch Eredivisie, crashed his Lamborghini into barriers on the M3 in Hampshire on the morning of Thursday, 28 May.

The 31-year-old was arrested and then released on bail pending further enquiries.

A Hampshire & Isle of Wight Constabulary spokesman said: "A driver will appear in court next month to face charges following a collision on the M3.

"Raheem Sterling, 31, from Berkshire, has been charged for the following offences: dangerous driving, possession of nitrous oxide for wrongful inhalation, failing to provide a specimen.

"The charges come following a single vehicle collision, involving a Lamborghini, on the M3 southbound, close to the Minley Interchange [Hampshire], on 28 May, 2026.

"No other vehicles were involved and no injuries were reported. Mr Sterling is due to appear at Basingstoke magistrates court on 15 September."

Police suspected Sterling of "driving a vehicle whilst unfit through drugs," but that has not been included in the charges.

In May a source close to Sterling told BBC Sport there was "no proof" of drugs in his system.

The source added the player had faced "an extremely tough couple of years" and had been made to "feel worthless" and "forgotten about".

Sterling has been without a club since leaving Dutch side Feyenoord at the end of last season.

He joined Feyenoord in February on a short-term contract after leaving Chelsea by mutual consent.

Chelsea paid £47.5m to sign Sterling from Manchester City in 2022, where he had won four Premier League titles, five League Cups and one FA Cup in seven years.

In 2024 the former Liverpool winger joined Arsenal on loan, but upon returning to Chelsea in 2025 was exiled from the first-team squad and made to train separately.

Sterling earned 82 England caps between 2012 and 2022, and appeared at three World Cups and two European Championships.

articles.title: Cafú, Zanetti y Roberto Carlos muestran su apoyo a Infantino
articles.standfirst: Leyendas del fútbol se ponen de lado del polémico presidente de la FIFA
articles.summary: Leyendas del fútbol se ponen de lado del polémico presidente de la FIFA
articles.body: Leyendas del fútbol como los brasileños Cafú y Roberto Carlos y el argentino Javier Zanetti han mostrado su apoyo al presidente de la FIFA, Gianni Infantino, en el centro de la polémica por su plan de vender a inversores privados una participación de los derechos del Mundial, que finalmente se vio obligado a retirar. "En los últimos diez años hemos hemos sido testigos de la labor realizada por la FIFA y el presidente Infantino para lograr una representación de los futbolistas en el mundo del futbol, algo que antes no existía", escribieron en las últimas horas en redes sociales exjugadores como Cafú, campeón del mundo en 1994 y 2002, o el exinternacional argentino Zanetti, actual vicepresidente del Inter de Milán, entre otros. El escrito, que apoya también Roberto Carlos, compañero de Cafú en la selección brasileña, y que han publicado asimismo otros jugadores, como los argentinos Esteban Cambiasso y Javier Pastore, se publica días después de que otros campeones del mundo reclamasen un "cambio necesario" al frente del fútbol. En esta ocasión, Cafú y Zanetti aseguran: "Se ha dado voz y un lugar en nuestro deporte a jugadores a través de participación en comités, proytectos y grupos de trabajo. Nuestras opiniones son escuchadas y muchas inicitaivas en beneficio del futbol se moldean gracias a nuestras reflexiones, ideas, planes y participación". Las leyendas sudamericanas se muestran "comprometidas a seguir llevando la esperanza" que ofrece el mundo para "transformar vidas, mejorar sociedades y ampliar las oportunidades para todos en el mundo". "Seguiremos dispuestos a apoyar la gran evolución que ha experimentado nuestro deporte en la última década para que continúe llegando y beneficiando a personas de todos los países donde se juega al fútbol", concluyen, con un apoyo rotundo a la labor del máximo mandatario de la FIFA. Infantino, que aspira a continuar al frente de la FIFA en el Congreso previsto para marzo de 2027, está siendo muy cuestionado en las últimas semanas, sobre todo por la UEFA, la Confederación Asiática de Fútbol (AFC) y la de Norte, Centroamérica y el Caribe (Concacaf), por el proyecto para vender a inversores privados una participación del 20 % de los derechos comerciales del Mundial. El mensaje de las leyendas sudamericanas llega después de campeones del mundo como los franceses Emmanuel Petit, Bixente Lizarazu y Robert Pires, y leyendas como el marfileño Didier Drogba reclamaran un "cambio necesario" al frente del fútbol porque "el poder ha nublado la capacidad del actual liderazgo para distinguir entre sus propios intereses y lo que realmente es mejor para el fútbol". "Los acontecimientos recientes han hecho imposible seguir guardando silencio. Ya basta", afirmaron estos últimos en una carta difundida también en redes sociales.

articles.standfirst: Mourinho regresa al Bernabéu ante el último campéon de Copa
articles.summary: Mourinho regresa al Bernabéu ante el último campéon de Copa
articles.body: El 1 de junio de 2013 fue la última vez que Jose Mourinho dirigió un partido del Real Madrid en el estadio Santiago Bernabéu. Después de más de 13 años, el entrenador de Setúbal vuelve a sentarse en el banquill del equipo local de Chamartín. Sin en Santiago ya en el nombre del estadio después de todo ese tiempo, el Madrid 2.0 de Mourinho se estrena en casa ante la Real Sociedad de Matarazzo, el equipo que la temporada pasada se llevó la Copa. Se presentan los blancos con las buenas sensaciones del triunfo logrado en la casa del Espanyol con el gol de Carlos Espí en el suspiro final. La Real, por su parte, abrió la temporada con derrota, en el campo del Betis. Con los mismos canteranos en la lista que los del viaje a Barcelona (Mestre, Mario Rivas, Cestero y Alexis Cirias), el Madrid tiene las mismas bajas: Endrick, Militao, Mendy, Thiago, Rodrygo, Asencio y Tchouaméni. Por parte del equipo vasco las bajas por lesión son tres: Odriozola, Gorrotxategi y Marín. Antes de que ruede la pelota, el Bernabéu rendirá homenaje a su campeón del mundo el pasado 19 de julio y uno de los fichajes de la temporada: Cucurella. En ese acto también se homenajeará a Oyarzabal, también campeón y máximo goleador de España en la Copa del Mundo.. Real Madrid: Courtois; Trent, Konaté, Rüdiger, Cucurella; Camavinga, Valverde; Güler, Bellingham, Vinicius; Mbappé. articles.title: Newcastle transfer news: Nico Gonzalez deal agreed with Man City for £52m
articles.summary: Newcastle United agree a deal worth up to £52m for Manchester City midfielder Nico Gonzalez.
articles.body:
Newcastle United have agreed a deal worth up to £52m for Manchester City midfielder Nico Gonzalez.

Newcastle have signed players exclusively from the continent up to this point in the window, but the club have recognised the need to add some Premier League experience after losing Bruno Guimaraes, Sandro Tonali, Anthony Gordon and Kieran Trippier in recent months.

Gonzalez has only spent a season-and-a-half in the Premier League after signing from Porto, but the 24-year-old fits the age profile Newcastle have been targeting as someone who could still develop further under head coach Matthias Jaissle.

The Spaniard previously said he "did not want to leave" the Etihad , but Manchester City subsequently agreed an £85.6m deal for Lille midfielder Ayyoub Bouaddi, having already signed Elliot Anderson from Nottingham Forest for £116m.

Gonzalez was an unused substitute at the weekend as Manchester City came from behind to defeat Bournemouth 2-1 in manager Enzo Maresca's first Premier League game in charge of the club.

He will become the fourth senior midfielder to leave City this summer after Bernardo Silva, Rodri and Tijjani Reijnders.

Analysis - Jaissle set to get his wish with Gonzalez

Although Newcastle 's young side came within seconds of defeating Liverpool on the opening weekend, there was always going to be work to do before the window shut on 1 September.

Newcastle have made six signings so far this summer in goalkeepers Lukas Hornicek and Ewen Jaouen, defender Amar Dedic, midfielders Aladji Bamba and Sean Steur and forward Bazoumana Toure.

But Jaissle made it clear that "adjustments need to be done and will be" in an interview with BBC Sport last week.

After reluctantly selling talisman Guimaraes to Arsenal , Gonzalez possesses the qualities Newcastle have been looking for in the middle of the park.

This is a player who would have been potentially out of reach not so long ago.

Of those midfielders who played a minimum of 900 minutes in Europe's top five leagues last season, Gonzalez led the way for high turnovers per game (2.13).

He also ranked in the Premier League's top five midfielders for line-breaking passes per match (12).

Those traits - in and out of possession - could make Gonzalez an invaluable addition as he is handed a greater role at St James' Park.

articles.title: El mercado entra en su cuenta atrás
articles.standfirst: Los clubes tienen una semana para cerrar medio centenar de operaciones
articles.summary: Los clubes tienen una semana para cerrar medio centenar de operaciones
articles.body: Entramos en la recta final del mercado y llegan las prisas para los equipos que no han hecho sus deberes este verano. LaLiga, como es habitual las últimas temporadas para la mayoría de los equipos, no está por la labor de hacer grandes desembolsos como sucede en la Premier, cuyos equipos reciben unos derechos de televisión más repartidos que aquí. Basta decir que los diez fichajes más caros de este verano los han hecho el Real Madrid (cuatro), Barcelona (tres) y Atlético (tres). El resto tiene que cuadrar cuentas como si jugaran en otra liga. Estas son las principales necesidades de los equipos a falta de una semana para el cierre. El mercado está cerrado para el Alavés, que sólo buscará algún fichaje en el caso de que sufra alguna pérdida a lo largo de la próxima semana. En ese sentido, el club se hará fuerte para retener a Antonio Blanco y Ángel Pérez, los dos jugadores que más intereses han despertado en las últimas semanas. El Athletic tiene decidido no hacer fichajes y sus únicas incorporaciones son los que jugaron cedidos el pasado curso -dos de ellos fueron titulares en el debut- y los que durante la campaña puedan promocionar desde el filial. Perder el tren europeo provoca un ajuste en los gastos. Mateu trabaja para fichar dos jugadores ofensivos. Un 9 (Nico Jackson es la opción principal) y el regreso de Nico González son los objetivos de un Atlético que trabaja también para la salida de cuatro futbolistas. Giménez y Lemar (los dos más complicados por sus altas nóminas), así como Carlos Martín y Obed Vargas, a los que se les busca destino cedidos. El Barça tiene varios asuntos pendientes. Sigue buscando un delantero centro (Julián Alvarez o el plan B) y también un defensa. Puede ser un defensa central o un lateral izquierdo. La llegada del zaguero estará determinada por algunas de las dos salidas de la defensa que se hablan: Balde y Koundé. Los dos que se marcharán seguro son Marc Casadó y Héctor Fort. Tras la llegada de Troy Parrott a la delantera para competir con Cucho Hernández, el Betis trabaja para intentar hacerle espacio salarial a Dani Ceballos y a un centrocampista de corte defensivo. El preferido por Pellegrini es Sofyan Amrabat, que ya conoce el club, pero las limitaciones económicas complican su regreso. Para poder firmar a los dos, Manu Fajardo busca destino a Iker Losada, Gonzalo Petit, Pablo García o Nelson Deossa. Con la llegada de Couhaib Driouech, al Celta le restarían dos últimos fichajes por realizar, según las necesidades que el propio Claudio Giráldez expresó públicamente. Un central derecho, de rendimiento inmediato, y un mediocentro. Por este orden, según prioridad, y con el valencianista André Almeida próximo. En el capítulo de salidas, queda por encontrar destino a Carles Pérez. El Deportivo busca en este final de mercado apuntalar la defensa y el mediocampo. Un central y un ‘6’ con experiencia son las peticiones de Antonio Hidalgo que tendrá a su disposición a Adama Traoré en unas horas. El extremo ex del Barça coincidirá de nuevo o con Aubameyang, ya que juntos jugaron en el cuadro blaugrana. El central es el que más necesidad tiene para el cuerpo técnico deportivista. Sonaron Juan Jesús, Zezé, Llorente… pero con la inminente salida de Barcia esa línea se queda corta de efectivos. A diferencia de la mayoría de temporadas con Bragarnik a los mandos, el Elche llega a las fechas finales del mercado con menos necesidades (al menos, en cuanto a número). La carencia principal es un lateral/carrilero izquierdo, donde Anselmi sólo cuenta con Germán Valera. La dirección deportiva también trabaja en el fichaje de un portero que compita con Dituro e Iturbe. No puede descartarse que el club ilicitano refuerce su ataque. Además, podría necesitar un central de alto nivel, ante el riesgo de clausulazo por Affengruber. El cierre de mercado del conjunto perico pasa por la incorporación de un extremo izquierdo. Una posición que parece casi segura para Bryan Zaragoza, que se trata del nombre que habría elegido Monchi para el club. El gaditano está tranquilo en el aspecto de salidas, sobre todo, de nombres como Roberto Fernández, con el runrún de la Premier. A su vez, el club perico cuenta con los jugadores que han vuelto de cesión para esta temporada: Roger Hinojo, Marcos Fernández, Rafel Bauzá y Javi Hernández. El Getafe tiene unos días ajetreados en clave mercado. Toni Muñoz tiene aún que dar salida a tres jugadores (Berrocal, Neyou y Javi Muñoz), aunque podría incluso salir otro nombre si llega una buena oferta. En clave llegadas, el club busca seguir reforzando varias posiciones. Un central, mínimo un mediocentro y un delantero es lo que tiene que traer el equipo, además de no descartar a alguien en banda. Todo, si sólo salen los tres primeros nombres; si no, el equipo buscará sustituto ante otras eventuales salidas. El mercado de fichajes del Levante no está ni cerca de cerrarse. Durante esta última semana, se espera la salida de un hombre fuerte en el vestuario como Carlos Álvarez, que estaría dispuesto a marcharse para que el equipo de Orriols pueda hacer caja. Las principales urgencias de Luís Castro se centran en la delantera y en la defensa. Se busca un goleador para poder equilibrar la salida de Carlos Espí y una posible venta de Etta Eyong, en la rampa de salida desde inicios de verano. Y también se precisa un marcador, tan necesario tras la marcha de Matías Moreno, Matturo y Unai Elgezabal. El Málaga busca dos piezas en la recta final del mercado de fichajes. Los blanquiazules quieren a un lateral izquierdo, puesto que ha quedado hueco tras la salida de Dani Sánchez, y un mediocentro que tenga capacidad de jugar en la posición de central. El elegido es Nemanja Gudelj, pero las negociaciones aún no están cerradas. Con estos dos movimientos el Málaga se iría hasta las siete caras nuevas en el mercado del verano de su regreso a Primera, una cifra que ya adelantó el director deportivo Loren Juarros a comienzos del periodo estival. El equipo rojillo, tras el ‘no’ fichaje de Kambwala y la posible marcha de Aitor Fernández, sigue a expensas de realizar entre dos y tres fichajes. Uno en la portería de darse esta salida y uno o dos jugadores de campo, aunque dependerá de otras posibles salidas como la de Enzo Boyomo, pretendido por distintos equipos. Mucho trabajo para los últimos días. De todas las incorporaciones están pendientes de las salidas de Salinas, Puerta y Sergio, que tienen ofertas pero de momento no se acercan a las pretensiones del club. El Racing necesita un lateral derecho, un central, uno o dos laterales izquierdos, un eje, un extremo derecho y un delantero centro (siempre que salga Arana). Parecen cerca de fichar esta misma semana Gorosabel, procedente del Athletic, y Matteo Prati, centrocampista del Cagliari, cuya llegada parece inminente. Las oficinas están echando humo. Después de los fichajes de Kumbulla y Tsitaishvili el cuadro franjirrojo ha dejado los deberes para la última semana y están ultimando los fichajes de Gnangoro Bouare (falta la oficialidad) y de un jugador que cubra esa demarcación en el lateral izquierdo que ha dejado Pep Chavarría con su marcha al Chelsea. En estos momentos, es Adriá Pedrosa la apuesta del cuadro franjirrojo. Sin embargo, tal y como dijo Beñat San José en rueda de prensa, el Rayo Vallecano está atento al mercado y si hay alguna oportunidad o salida de última hora que podría volver a activarse. Tras la llegada de Mou y seis fichajes, el club blanco considera que ya ha hecho los deberes en el mercado... salvo accidente. Sólo una circunstancia inesperada en forma de salida no prevista o lesión de importancia activaría nuevamente la maquinaria del Madrid, satisfecho con su verano. En todo caso, queda una semana por delante en la que puede haber sorpresas. No ha realizado ninguna incorporación, bien porque sus ofertas han sido insuficientes, como recientemente por el brasileño Jonathan Jesus, bien porque al final no ha estado segura de ficharlo, como con Nayef Aguerd. Matarazzo quiere un central, preferiblemente zurdo, y un lateral derecho, puesto para el que suena Héctor Fort. Además, si queda dinero, la idea es lograr un futbolista estilo Guedes, es decir, que pueda moverse por todas las posiciones de ataque. La hoja de ruta ideal del Sevilla pasaría por firmar tres o cuatro jugadores y otras tantas salidas. La venta de Rubén Vargas y/o Agoumé le daría el impulso definitivo a la planificación de José Ignacio Navarro. La prioridad es la llegada del tercer delantero. Un extremo y otro centrocampista también son necesarios. En cuanto se cierre el fichaje del lateral derecho del Girona Arnau Martínez al Valencia le quedarían dos posiciones por intentar reforzar, aunque la recta final del mercado va a depender también de las posibles salidas de André Almeida y Danjuma. A Corberán le gustaría contar con un jugador de ataque, no delantero centro, y de hecho no se olvida de Largie Ramazani, sin dorsal en el Leeds. Además, se busca un central teniendo en cuenta el historial de lesiones de Diakhaby, ahora recuperado, y las bajas de Copete, sin fecha de regreso, y De Haas, que tiene para un mes.  El Villarreal ha decidido finalmente no apurar hasta última hora del mercado y acometer el fichaje del centrocampista que cierre definitivamente su plantilla. Y este será Nathan Saliba, canadiense de 22 años que llega procedente del Anderlecht y por el que la entidad castellonense abonará 15 millones de euros. El futbolista llegará en las próximas horas a España para completar los trámites y firmar por el conjunto azulejero. Internacional con su país y mundialista este pasado verano, en el “submarino” volverá a verse las caras con dos compatriotas como son Tajon Buchanan y Tani Oluwaseyi. De esta forma completará un centro del campo en el que Iñigo Pérez ya tiene a su disposición a Pape Gueye, Comesaña y los canteranos Diatta y Carlos Macià.

articles.title: Brighton & Hove Albion sign Algerian left-back Jaouen Hadjam
articles.summary: The 23-year-old joins from Swiss champions Young Boys on a five-year deal, making him the third Algerian in the league.
articles.body:
Algerian defender Jaouen Hadjam has joined Brighton & Hove Albion from Swiss champions Young Boys for an undisclosed fee on a contract until 2031, the Premier League club has confirmed.

Brighton announced the signing on Tuesday with a video showing the left-back sipping mint tea in a cafe.

Hadjam joins Manchester City’s Rayan Ait-Nouri and Hull City’s Mohamed El Bachir Belloumi as Algerian internationals playing in the Premier League.

Former Leicester City and Manchester City winger Riyad Mahrez is arguably the most famous and successful Algerian to have played in the league.

The Paris-born player represented France at youth level before switching allegiance to Algeria in 2023. He has earned 21 caps for his country.

Hadjam, 23, made 98 appearances for Young Boys in all competitions after joining the Swiss side from Ligue 1 club Nantes in 2024. He played in Paris Saint-Germain’s youth academy.

He was part of Algeria’s squad at the FIFA World Cup 2026, where he played in three of the team’s four matches.

Brighton started their league campaign by beating Europa League holders Aston Villa 4-0 on Sunday.

articles.standfirst: Te contamos a qué hora y dónde ver el partido de la jornada 1 de LaLiga EA Sports entre el Real Madrid y la Real Sociedad.
articles.summary: Te contamos a qué hora y dónde ver el partido de la jornada 1 de LaLiga EA Sports entre el Real Madrid y la Real Sociedad.
articles.body: Más de 13 años después, José Mourinho vuelve al banquillo del Bernabéu para dirigir un partido de fútbol.  Lo hará frente a la Real Sociedad, uno de los equipos de moda del fútbol español que, tras las llegada de Pellegrino Matarazzo en el pasado invierno, se ha convertido en uno de los equipos más fuertes de primera, Copa del Rey mediante.  El conjunto blanco llega tras vencer en el primer partido oficial de la temporada por 1-2 con gol en el descuento de Espí, en un duelo en el que los madridistas dominaron pero no fueron capaces de certificar los tres puntos hasta los minutos finales.  El partido, a pesar de ser el segundo oficial para ambos equipos, corresponde a la primera jornada de liga, aplazado por la llegada de los jugadores del Mundial. articles.title: Omar Marmoush: Tottenham agree loan for Manchester City forward
articles.summary: Tottenham agree a loan deal to sign Manchester City forward Omar Marmoush, with an obligation to make the deal permanent for £60m next summer.
articles.body:
Tottenham have agreed a loan deal to sign Manchester City forward Omar Marmoush, with an obligation to make the deal permanent for £60m next summer.

The 27-year-old Egypt international follows Savio from City to Spurs after the north London club signed the Brazilian for an initial fee of £75m on Tuesday.

Marmoush joined City from Eintracht Frankfurt for £59m last January but had to play second fiddle to Erling Haaland for much of his time at Etihad Stadium.

He was a second-half substitute in City's 3-0 Community Shield defeat by Arsenal and then an unused substitute in their Premier League opener on Saturday, a 2-1 home win over Bournemouth .

Spurs have already spent more than £312m this summer on transfers.

They have signed Mateus Fernandes from West Ham, Sandro Tonali from Newcastle and Jan Paul van Hecke from Brighton , while defenders Marcos Senesi and Andy Robertson, and goalkeeper Martin Dubravka, have arrived on free transfers.

Marmoush scored 16 goals in 62 appearances in all competitions for City following his move from Frankfurt.

Eight of those came in 36 appearances in 2025-26, but his Premier League involvement fell considerably.

He started only eight league games and played around 700 minutes, fewer than he managed after joining midway through the prior campaign.

His league return was three goals and three assists, with his 3.53 expected goals figure close to his actual scoring output. The issue was therefore not simply finishing.

Marmoush found himself competing for minutes in a side built around Haaland, while City further strengthened their attacking options.

Spurs forward Dominic Solanke has endured injury problems over the past 18 months, while team-mate Richarlison has entered the final year of his contract.

Marmoush is primarily a number nine, but he has rarely been confined to one role across the front line.

At Frankfurt he was used predominantly through the middle but also appeared as a second striker and from the left. City have followed a similar pattern, using him mainly as a central attacker while also deploying him from the flank and just behind another forward.

That flexibility could suit Spurs manager Roberto de Zerbi. His teams have often relied on forwards changing positions, dropping towards the ball and then attacking the space created when opponents are drawn out. Marmoush is comfortable doing both.

But in terms of global reach, support, and viewership, Bayern have always been chasing Real Madrid , Barcelona , and the Premier League giants. However, it looks like that is slowly changing.

Bayern's recent revival and extremely successful 2025/26 campaign seems to be reflected in their social media numbers as well (via @iMiaSanMia ).

articles.title: What can Baleba offer Man Utd?
articles.summary: Carlos Baleba's appeal lies less in creativity and more in his ability to win possession, cover ground and then carry his team forward.  Baleba averaged 6.7...
articles.body:
Carlos Baleba 's appeal lies less in creativity and more in his ability to win possession, cover ground and then carry his team forward.

His 2025-26 campaign was quieter than the previous one, but his 2024-25 numbers show why Manchester United have tracked him for so long. He ranked fourth among Premier League midfielders for possessions won in the middle third (107) and interceptions (46), was fifth for ball recoveries (197) and seventh for duels won (199).

That defensive output was matched by his ability to progress possession himself.

Baleba averaged 6.7 progressive carries per 90 minutes, with only three qualifying Premier League defensive midfielders recording more, while 2.9 of those carries travelled at least 10 metres.

His athleticism underpins that game as he reached a top speed of 34.5km/h in 2024-25, compared with 30.5km/h for Casemiro , and averaged 8.2 defensive actions per 90.

He is not necessarily the midfielder United would rely on to dictate possession. Only 11.8% of his passes were classed as line-breaking that season and 22.7% travelled forward - both below the average for central and defensive midfielders.

But that may make him complementary to United's other options rather than a direct alternative. Youri Tielemans can provide more of the progressive distribution, while Baleba offers defensive security and the ability to drive through midfield.

Alongside Kobbie Mainoo , he could take on more of the ball-winning and ground-covering work, while a partnership with Andrey Santos could allow Baleba greater freedom to operate box to box.

That versatility is reflected in his positioning as he spent 88% of his minutes last season as a defensive midfielder and 12% in central midfield, suggesting he can anchor the side or step forward depending on who plays alongside him.

United most commonly defended in a 4-2-2-2 last season under Michael Carrick, accounting for 55.9% of their out-of-possession shapes. Baleba's dynamism could be especially valuable in a system where central midfielders are asked to defend large spaces and stop counter-attacks.

There may, however, be an adaptation period.

Baleba is recovering from an ankle ligament injury suffered in pre-season and will need time to recover his match sharpness.

United have also looked to spend longer spells in possession under Carrick, progressing through midfield with quick combinations. Baleba's game is better suited to more open contests, but his passing profile suggests he may need time to adjust to greater responsibility in build-up.

His left foot and mobility should still make him a natural partner for players such as Tielemans or Bruno Fernandes . There is development ahead of him at 22, not least after last season's dip, but at his best Baleba combines defensive activity with the acceleration and carrying power to transform a turnover into an attack within seconds.

articles.title: Moyes' cup comments prompt fan questions
articles.summary: After Everton's CEO Angus Kinnear told me exclusively last week that the club's owners called last season "a failure" eyebrows were raised when David Moyes a...
articles.body:
After Everton 's CEO Angus Kinnear told me exclusively last week that the club's owners called last season "a failure " eyebrows were raised when David Moyes angrily insisted staying up in the Premier League is the more important aim.

The Friedkin Group were left unhappy when the first full season at Hill Dickinson Stadium ended without a trophy and no European qualification. I was told "appropriate pressure" was put on this summer as the American consortium bought Everton Football Club to win but flash forward just seven days and quotes have emerged from the manager that almost feel defeatist with just one game played.

Ahead of tonight's League Cup game at Preston David Moyes was asked how important the cups are to him this season and his answer has left fans irritated.

"Of course we all want to win the cups," he explained. "Yes the cups are hugely important, would it be more important than staying in the Premier League? I'll ask you the question: Is winning a cup more important than staying in the Premier League? What would your answer be?"

The tone of the Toffees boss has left some questioning if he is on the same page as the owners and the CEO. Last season there was frustration at the third round exits in both the League Cup and FA Cup with tactics fiercely criticised. Jordan Pickford was rested for the League Cup which saw supporters angered after seeing Newcastle end their trophy drought in the tournament the season before.

Evertonians deserve a cup run. For too long they have dragged their team over the line time and time again. They were the glue holding an increasingly fractured club together as PSR charges hit, points were deducted, favourite players sold and the club's hierarchy disappeared.

When The Friedkin Group took over at the end of 2024 it signalled much-needed stability and an end to the financial chaos that had become synonymous with the Toffees. They oversaw the move to a new stadium and have assured fans they are winners. The manager talking down the chance to hunt for a trophy for the first time in 31 years isn't the team talk supporters want to hear in the build up to a potential cup run. It now leads to questions around whether Moyes can be the man the owners are able trust to return Everton to a side that can fight it out for silverware and it has heaped even more pressure on tonight's trip to Deepdale.

articles.title: Raheem Sterling charged with dangerous driving after motorway crash
articles.summary: Former England forward Raheem Sterling has been charged with dangerous driving and possession of nitrous oxide after a crash involving a Lamborghini on the m...
articles.body:
Former England forward Raheem Sterling has been charged with dangerous driving and possession of nitrous oxide after a crash involving a Lamborghini on the motorway, police have said.

Hampshire and Isle of Wight Constabulary said the charges followed a single-vehicle collision on the M3 southbound, near Minley interchange, on May 28.

The 31-year-old is accused of dangerous driving, possession of nitrous oxide for wrongful inhalation and failing to provide a specimen.

The force said that no other vehicles were involved in the collision and no injuries were reported.

Sterling, from Berkshire, is due to appear at Basingstoke Magistrates' Court for a hearing on September 15.

He scored 20 goals in 82 appearances for England, helping Gareth Southgate's side reach the 2018 World Cup semi-finals and the final of Euro 2020.

He came through the academy at QPR before joining Liverpool , where he made his senior debut.

Sterling, who was born in Kingston, Jamaica, moved to Manchester City in 2015 and won four Premier League titles, five League Cups and the FA Cup in 2019.

He left for Chelsea in 2022 but after falling out of favour spent the 2024-25 season on loan at Arsenal .

After leaving Stamford Bridge, Sterling joined Dutch club Feyenoord on a short-term deal until the end of the season.

In the 2021 Queen's Birthday Honours, Sterling was made an MBE for services to racial equality in sport after fronting anti-racism and discrimination campaigns and speaking out strongly against racism on and off the pitch for several years.

It came amid controversy over England fans booing players taking the knee at matches as a gesture against intolerance.

articles.summary: The 50+1 rule has been a central pillar of German professional football since its introduction in 1998. In line with a member-led club culture and sustainabl...
articles.body:
The 50+1 rule has been a central pillar of German professional football since its introduction in 1998. In line with a member-led club culture and sustainable business models, it forms the basis of a unique characteristic that sets the Bundesliga apart significantly in international comparison.

Borussia Dortmund and its fans clearly stand by the 50+1 rule and its long-term preservation. We therefore expressly welcome the Bundeskartellamt's fundamental assessment.

We are convinced that the long-term success of German football can be ensured in this way. That is also why BVB firmly embedded this principle in its statutes and code of fundamental values many years ago.
